title: Respiration equation card
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: The periodic table (8F); breathing and respiration (8C)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 34 (Respiration equation card (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 34: Aerobic respiration. To understand how cells release energy from glucose using oxygen

questions.q: Why do muscle cells have many mitochondria?
questions.a: They need a lot of energy for contraction, released by respiration in mitochondria
questions.model: What do muscles need? Lots of energy. Where is energy released? Mitochondria. So more mitochondria, more energy.

questions.q: What are the products of aerobic respiration?
Name one use of the energy released.
Explain in the portal response box how a sandwich you eat helps your leg muscle move. Use: digestion, glucose, blood, oxygen, mitochondria. Starter: 'The bread is digested into...'
questions.a: The bread is digested into glucose, absorbed into the blood and carried to the muscle. Oxygen from the lungs is carried by red blood cells. In the mitochondria, glucose reacts with oxygen to release energy for contraction.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first link: 'The bread is digested into glucose in the small intestine.'

questions.q: Why does your breathing rate increase when you run?
questions.a: Muscles respire faster and need more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Plants also respire. Write their word equation and say when they do it.
questions.a: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water; all the time, day and night.

questions.q: Big question: what are your cells using energy for while you sit?
questions.a: Warmth, the heartbeat, the brain, growth and repair.
